correctness.rationale: The \(L\)-th Fourier coefficient of each squared STFT time slice has exactly one surviving window-overlap pair, so it equals \(f_{k+L}\overline{f_k}\overline{g_L}g_0\). Equal measurements force equal endpoint products. For nonvanishing signals, ratios satisfy \(r_{k+L}\overline{r_k}=1\) and hence \(r_{k+2L}=r_k\); \(\gcd(d,2L)=1\) makes the ratio constant, and the first relation makes it unimodular. The packaged verifier independently replays 106 finite parameter pairs and is explicitly not treated as proof.

value.rationale: The theorem removes a standard window-spectrum hypothesis for an entire natural signal class, not for an isolated example. The endpoint coefficient gives an explicit reconstruction and explains the odd-dimensional arithmetic mechanism. This provides a useful structural boundary for short-window STFT phase retrieval and directly advances the literature goal of weakening ambiguity-support assumptions.
